article_sentences: Transport associations argue that independent drivers, many of whom have bought their vehicles through bank loans, will struggle to compete with a company-backed fleet.
They have pointed to expenses such as monthly loan instalments, insurance, permits and vehicle maintenance, which drivers must bear regardless of how much they earn.
At least four taxi and transport associations have approached Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, seeking intervention over Green SM's proposed operations in Bengaluru.

In their representation, they have called for transparency on the permissions and licences granted to the company, along with an independent assessment of its potential impact on local transport operators.
"We welcome the transition towards environmentally sustainable transportation.
However, such a transition must be implemented in a fair, transparent and inclusive manner, without discriminating against local operators," the associations said.
Nataraj Sharma, president of the Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations, said local operators would find it difficult to match the proposed fares.
Speaking to TOI, Sharma said there were currently no state government regulations governing fares charged by electric taxis.
He added that Green SM could potentially offer rides for less than Rs 8 per km, while existing operators use petrol, diesel, CNG and LPG-powered vehicles.
"We will not be able to offer prices as low as them," he said.
The federation has also raised concerns about the company's access to corporate funding, bulk vehicle purchases, its own booking app and fleet-management systems.
It believes these advantages could put independent drivers under pressure to lower fares, even as they continue to pay their loan instalments and meet operating costs.

stories.title: Akvan intensifies into severe cyclone near Andhra coast
stories.summary: Visakhapatnam, Nov 18 : Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, looming over the central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a severe cyclone, and is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Friday. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) bulletin on Wednesday morning, the cyclonic storm moved very slowly north-northwestwards with the speed of three kmph during past six hours, intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lay centered at 0530 hours at about 580 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 650 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 730 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). Continuing to move north-northwestward, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of November 20, as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph. Prakhar Jain, Managing Director, Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority and Chief Executive Officer of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), said that the cyclone movement is being continuously monitored. Appropriate instructions are being issued to the district administrations. He said 13 teams of NDRF, 11 teams of SDRF and local fire brigades were ready for emergency relief operations. Due to the impact of Tapan, there will be very heavy rains in some places in coastal districts on Thursday and Friday. Heavy to very heavy rains are likely at isolated places. APSDMA has appealed to people in the coastal region not to leave their homes unless it is an emergency. Farmers have been advised to take precautionary measures in agricultural work. Meanwhile, Home Minister V. Anita reviewed the situation as 'Akvan' intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. Officials reported that 'Akvan' is moving at a sluggish pace of 3 km/h. It is expected to make landfall by the afternoon of Friday. Home Minister Anita directed the state machinery to remain on high alert for the next 48 hours. She directed officials to take measures to prevent loss of life and property. The cyclone is likely to impact the North Andhra region. The public has been advised to remain vigilant. The Home Minister said residents in coastal areas should avoid stepping out unless absolutely necessary. Residents in low-lying areas must move to relief centres as soon as instructed by the authorities, she said. (IANS)

article_sentences: The review, to be held in Agra, is part of the Election Commission's preparations for Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa.

A team of senior Election Commission officials will review Uttar Pradesh’s preparedness for the Assembly elections on November 19 as part of a phased assessment ahead of polls expected early next year, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

Officials told PTI that the team, led by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, had recently visited Meerut to assess the preparedness of election officials in some divisions of western Uttar Pradesh.
The review in the state is being conducted in phases.
The Election Commission has completed its review visits to Uttarakhand, Manipur and Punjab, while a visit to Goa is being planned.
While recently ordering a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states, the poll body noted that Assembly elections in the five states could take place "early next year."
The term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly ends on May 22, 2027.

article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces, with rewards of up to ₹1.5 lakh for individual weapons and sanctioning powers extending to ₹1 crore.
The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

According to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the reward amount will depend on the type and number of weapons recovered, including automatic and semi-automatic firearms, other weapons and ammunition.
The government said Maoists had, over the years, looted weapons belonging to State security forces during attacks on police stations and police personnel.

While existing provisions provide rewards for information leading to the arrest of Maoists and additional financial assistance to those surrendering with weapons, there was no specific provision for rewarding individuals who helped recover weapons previously looted from security forces.
The Home Department subsequently proposed a separate reward mechanism to facilitate the recovery of these weapons, which received Cabinet approval on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Under the scheme, Superintendents of Police will have the authority to sanction rewards of up to ₹10 lakh, while the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Gadchiroli Range, can approve amounts exceeding ₹10 lakh and up to ₹25 lakh.

Rewards exceeding ₹25 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh will require approval from the Special Inspector General of Police, Anti-Naxal Operations, while the Additional Director General of Police (Special Operations) will be authorised to approve rewards exceeding ₹50 lakh and up to ₹1 crore.
The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities.

In its statement, the government said coordinated efforts by the Centre and the State had weakened the influence of Maoist organisations in the region, particularly in Gadchiroli and Gondia, which it described as having become Naxal-free.
The government also said several development projects were being implemented in these districts as part of efforts to transform areas previously affected by Left-wing extremism.

article_sentences: The Delhi Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved one-time financial assistance of ₹1 lakh each to around 500 Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) issuing centres for improving their infrastructure, as per the Chief Minister’s Office.
The assistance will support the upgradation and modernisation of these centres and the government is expected to spend approximately ₹5 crore on the initiative.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that controlling air pollution in Delhi remains one of the government’s key priorities.
“Modern infrastructure, transparent testing procedures and effective monitoring are essential to ensuring cleaner air.

Equipping vehicle pollution testing centres with modern facilities and bringing uniformity to their operations will strengthen the government’s efforts to control pollution,” Ms. Gupta said, adding that the aim is to make the PUC testing system more organised, transparent and reliable.

The CM said that stronger CCTV surveillance will make it easier to monitor the testing process, enhancing transparency and accountability at the centres and will also strengthen public confidence in the PUC certification system.

A CAG report tabled in the Delhi Assembly in April last year had said there were significant “discrepancies” in the Pollution Under Control (PUC) certification system, and many vehicle owners were not getting their vehicles checked as per norms.
These centres check vehicle emissions and issue Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs).

The unorganised development of the PUCC centres has resulted in a lack of uniformity in infrastructure, testing facilities, signboards, external appearance and monitoring arrangements, making effective supervision difficult, the CMO said in a statement.
“Inadequate CCTV coverage has also led to allegations of improper issuance of PUCCs and other irregularities.
The scheme aims to address these shortcomings by bringing all authorised PUC centres in line with uniform prescribed standards and making the testing system more transparent and organised.
Where a PUC centre tests all three categories of vehicles, it is technically treated as a single centre,” the statement said.

stories.headline: Trump faces key China issues ahead of meeting with Xi
stories.title: Trump faces key China issues ahead of meeting with Xi
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 18 : US President Donald Trump heads into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week amid divisions within his administration over restricting China's access to advanced technology, even as Washington and Beijing pursue cooperation on artificial intelligence risks and seek to preserve their trade truce. The White House schedule places their bilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, followed by three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. China's Foreign Ministry has separately confirmed the trilateral meeting for November 19. The New York Times reported Tuesday that the disagreement over technology restrictions extends beyond Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and much of the National Security Council staff have supported broader limits on China's access to advanced AI chips, while Lutnick pushed for a softer approach, the newspaper reported, citing current and former officials familiar with the discussions. The Times also reported concerns among advocates of a tougher China policy that Trump could reverse recently announced restrictions or use them as bargaining material in talks with Xi. Those concerns do not establish that Trump intends to offer such a concession. Former national security advisor H.R. McMaster told the newspaper that Trump's confidence in his negotiating ability could undermine a consistent approach to Beijing. "I think President Trump is often impeded by his belief that he can get the deal nobody else can get," McMaster said. The administration announced restrictions Monday aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced American computing technology remotely through overseas data centres. But technology competition is only one part of the relationship. The Washington Post highlighted parallel efforts to manage AI risks through model-testing cooperation and an incident-notification channel. Bessent said Washington and Beijing had begun a dialogue intended to reduce shared risks and prevent misunderstandings. He outlined plans to exchange practices for evaluating advanced AI models before their release and to establish a direct channel for the two countries to alert each other about any serious incidents involving their models. Bessent also described the administration's broader economic approach: "our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple." Critical-mineral supplies present another test of whether diplomatic agreements can produce dependable commercial outcomes -- an issue with direct relevance to India's manufacturing ambitions. A November 10 analysis by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies found that US imports of the covered rare-earth compounds and metals from China averaged 19.3 metric tonnes a month between November 2025 and September 2026. That compared with a monthly average of 76.8 metric tonnes before Beijing's April 2025 restrictions, a decline of about 75 per cent. India also depends heavily on Chinese supplies of permanent magnets. An Indian government background paper published in December 2025 said China accounted for between 84.8 per cent and 90.4 per cent of India's permanent-magnet imports by quantity during the financial years 2022-23 through 2024-25. India has approved a Rs 7,280 crore scheme intended to establish domestic manufacturing capacity of 6,000 metric tons annually for sintered rare-earth permanent magnets. The materials are important for electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics, aerospace and defence. Trump's engagement with India and other regional partners adds a strategic dimension to the China visit. At a November 9 CSIS briefing, Edgard Kagan, the organisation's senior adviser and Freeman chair in China studies, said a Quad meeting before Trump's China talks would remind Beijing of Washington's significant regional relationships. The Quad leaders met in Manila on Tuesday. They discussed Iran, safe navigation and energy security, and affirmed cooperation on critical-mineral supply chains. The Shenzhen talks will take place against that combination of strategic competition, commercial dependence and efforts to manage technological risks. (IANS)

New Delhi: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin will visit Jalandhar on Wednesday to flag off a 'Samrasta Sankalp Yatra' amid preparations to strengthen the party's position in Punjab ahead of the Assembly elections, scheduled for 2027.
This comes as the BJP is celebrating the 650th birth anniversary of Saint Shiromani Guru Ravidas as a year-long national festival.
"This mega campaign was launched on July 29, 2026, on the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima from Kashi (Uttar Pradesh).

So far, under this campaign, nearly 29,000 'Kalash Vandana Yatras' have been taken out, more than 30,000 saints have been reached out to, and 'Samras Deep Mahotsavs' have been organised at 51,000 locations to spread the message of social harmony (Samrasta)," the statement added.
Continuing this nationwide observance, the 16-day 'Samrasta.
Sankalp Yatra' will be organised from November 18 to December 3.

After being flagged off by Nabin from Jalandhar, the Yatra will pass through seven states and Union Territories -- Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Chandigarh, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh -- covering a total distance of 2,402 kilometres before concluding in Kashi on December 3, the BJP said.

During the Yatra, more than 100 small public meetings and 17 major events will be organised, where Union Ministers and national party office-bearers will participate to propagate Saint Ravidas' vision of 'Begumpura' (a realm without sorrow) and social equality among the masses, the statement said.
Nabin will also offer prayers at places of worship during his day-long engagements.
Following his arrival in Jalandhar, Nabin will proceed to Sant Shiromani Guru Ravidas Maharaj Mandir at Dera Sachkhand Ballan to offer prayers.
He will also address supporters on the occasion at Raipur village, located near Dera Sachkhand Ballan on the Jalandhar-Pathankot GT Road, a BJP statement said.

stories.title: J-K CM inaugurates, lays foundation for 13 projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in Poonch
stories.summary: Mendhar, Nov 18: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday laid the foundation stones and inaugurated 13 development projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in the border town of Mendhar in Poonch district, aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public service delivery. The projects cover key sectors, including power, flood protection, road connectivity, education and water supply, an official spokesman said. He said the projects include the laying of foundation stones for a 50 MVA Grid Sub-Station at Mendhar and flood protection works along Mendhari Nallah, besides key infrastructure projects in road connectivity, education and water supply. During the programme, the chief minister also flagged off Jammu and Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation (SRTC) bus services on three new routes and two new water tankers to improve public transport and drinking water supply in Mendhar. The spokesman said the chief minister's visit underscored the government's commitment to strengthening essential infrastructure, improving public services and accelerating development in remote and border areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
